data.gender_notes: Probo is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'probus', meaning 'honorable, virtuous, or respected'. In Christian tradition, Probo is the name of several saints. The name Probo carries the meaning “Esteemed, Respected” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Probo usually hope their child will grow to embody esteemed, respected and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes devotion and respect for one's faith.
data.etymology: Probo belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Esteemed, Respected.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Probo total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_greek.name: Πρόβο

in_latin.name: Probo

historical_references.reference: Probo Aurelius Valerius, a Roman emperor who ruled from AD 276 to 282. He was known as 'Probus' due to his piety and religious devotion. He undertook military campaigns against the Sassanians in the east and the Germanic tribes in the north, and built several roads and bridges throughout the empire.

historical_references.reference: Probus of Aquitaine, a bishop of the late 5th century. He is best known for his opposition to the Arian heresy and his role in the Councils of Agde and Orléans. He was also a prolific writer, producing several important theological texts.
historical_references.context: Christianity, opposition to Arian heresy, Councils of Agde and Orléans, theological writings
